# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1753._

> ℹ️ **7 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a confirming endpoint report still leaves the window "unverified"**

`_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes into the registry only when `detected != model.contextWindow`. When the endpoint's report CONFIRMS the carried catalog value (the common case for well-catalogued models), nothing is published, so `registry.isVerified(model)` stays false and the AC6 badge on every `task_status` pressure row marks that window unverified — even though the provider just verified it.

Since `publish` with the same value is a behavioral no-op (`windowFor` returns what the model already carries) and `withRegisteredContextWindow` short-circuits on `registered == model.contextWindow`, publishing unconditionally is free and makes the verification ladder honest:

```dart
if (detected != null) {
  _replaceModelLimits(
    contextWindow: detected == model.contextWindow ? null : detected,
    windowSource: ContextWindowSource.endpointReport,
  );
  ...
}
```

(with the publish reading `detected` rather than the rebuilt window, or by moving the publish next to the `detected != null` check). Purely a truth-in-UI fix; no behavior change.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

`withRegisteredContextWindow` rebuilds `Model` field-by-field (18 fields) to swap one value. This is the second hand-copy of the full field list in the codebase (`_replaceModelLimits` in `provider_models.dart` is the first); `Model` has no `copyWith`, so the next field added to `Model` (they do get added — `timeoutScopeLabel`, `capabilityNotes`, `connectTimeout`, `streamIdleTimeout` are all recent) must be remembered in **two** hand-copies plus anywhere else this pattern lands, or it is silently dropped (the analyzer cannot catch a missing named argument on a constructor that doesn't require it).

Cheapest insurance while you are here: add `Model copyWith({int? contextWindow})` (or a focused `withContextWindow(int)`) next to the class and use it in both sites — then the field list lives exactly once, next to the class it mirrors.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "smol summarizer resolves the same number" claim is not implemented**

The registry's header doc says "main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx meter resolve the same number" — but the smol summarizer never touches the registry: `_compactChildIfNeeded` passes `rolesResolver?.resolveRole(smolModelRole)` straight into `AutoCompactorSources(smolModel:)` unwrapped, and the CLI's main compaction wiring does the same. Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1753
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1753
- **Title**: gh-1742 [GOAL] Truthful context pressure: compaction keyed to observed usage + honest windows (subagents ride fictitious windows today)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1742` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +2429
- **Deletions**: -290
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:28:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T20:41:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1742
### What changed
Context-pressure governance is now keyed to observed provider usage instead of the chars/4 estimate alone: pressure decisions reconcile `max(estimate, last observed input+cacheRead)`, all compaction surfaces resolve one shared per-model window registry, and headroom scales with the window instead of a flat 16k reserve.

### Key decisions
- New pure decision core `assessContextPressure` / `reconcileContextTokens` / `lastObservedContextTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/context_pressure.dart`): observed wins over estimate, estimate fills gaps; no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior.
- `ContextWindowRegistry` (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart`): one window per `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` shared by main, children, and the meter; `contextWindowCap` now applies to children too (previously `null` in `_compactChildIfNeeded`).
- `CompactionSettings.forWindow` proportional: reserve = `window/16` clamped to `[12.5k, 64k]`, keepRecent = `window/8` clamped to `[20k, 128k]` — a 1M window keeps ≥64k headroom instead of 1.6%. A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before.
- The CLI joins the shared registry: `AgentCli` owns one, `_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes endpoint reports, `/model-edit` publishes user pins, and `SubagentServices` hands it to the `task` tool — children spawned after a detection ride the served window, not the advertised one.
- Child compaction (`TaskExecutor._compactChildIfNeeded`): observed-over-headroom forces the pass through a per-child latch (`_forcedObservedAt`) so a stale pre-fold anchor cannot re-force every boundary.
- Fixed a real hole this exposed in `AutoCompactorFactory`: a FORCED structured run whose own estimate sat under the token trigger did zero passes yet reported `ok`, skipping the classic fallback — forced (usage- or message-cap-triggered) zero-pass outcomes now fall through to the classic engine, whose forced semantics actually run the summarizer.
- `SubagentHandle` pressure stamps carry `observedTokens` + `windowVerified` (AC6 badge basis for `task_status`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction test/task test/agent test/cli
```

<details><summary>Verification notes</summary>

- `test/compaction test/task test/agent test/hosts`: 1204 passed, 0 failed. `test/cli`: 3920 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (including the resume-parity marathon set and HEP compaction frames).
- The shared `browser_ext`/`integration` suites (subprocess/PTY-heavy, outside this ticket's surface) show runner-load flakiness (subprocess 2-minute timeouts) on this shared runner; no gh-1742-touched path is involved — CI on the PR is the authoritative gate for those.
</details>

<details><summary>AC coverage</summary>

- **AC1/AC5** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — reconciliation, forced-vs-estimate channels, edge `==` line.
- **AC2** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — registry published post-"detection" → child rides the registered window (131,072-vs-478k repro), cap clamps children.
- **AC2 (CLI)** `test/cli/agent_cli_context_window_registry_test.dart` — `/model-edit` publishes the pin; a child spawned after a registry entry resolves the registered window, not the carried one.
- **AC3** `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` — reserve/keep tables 8k→2M, clamps, monotonicity, legacy-parity floor in the ≤64k band.
- **AC4/REG-1** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — gh_1122 (never later than legacy at ≤200k) and kimi (−5% drift cannot delay the observed channel) regression pins at the real fixture scales.
- **AC5 IT** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — scripted gateway reporting `total_tokens` that excludes the cached prefix: estimate stays under the trigger while the forced pass demonstrably runs a compaction LLM call and lands a session compaction record.
</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1753._

> ℹ️ **7 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a confirming endpoint report still leaves the window "unverified"**

`_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes into the registry only when `detected != model.contextWindow`. When the endpoint's report CONFIRMS the carried catalog value (the common case for well-catalogued models), nothing is published, so `registry.isVerified(model)` stays false and the AC6 badge on every `task_status` pressure row marks that window unverified — even though the provider just verified it.

Since `publish` with the same value is a behavioral no-op (`windowFor` returns what the model already carries) and `withRegisteredContextWindow` short-circuits on `registered == model.contextWindow`, publishing unconditionally is free and makes the verification ladder honest:

```dart
if (detected != null) {
  _replaceModelLimits(
    contextWindow: detected == model.contextWindow ? null : detected,
    windowSource: ContextWindowSource.endpointReport,
  );
  ...
}
```

(with the publish reading `detected` rather than the rebuilt window, or by moving the publish next to the `detected != null` check). Purely a truth-in-UI fix; no behavior change.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

`withRegisteredContextWindow` rebuilds `Model` field-by-field (18 fields) to swap one value. This is the second hand-copy of the full field list in the codebase (`_replaceModelLimits` in `provider_models.dart` is the first); `Model` has no `copyWith`, so the next field added to `Model` (they do get added — `timeoutScopeLabel`, `capabilityNotes`, `connectTimeout`, `streamIdleTimeout` are all recent) must be remembered in **two** hand-copies plus anywhere else this pattern lands, or it is silently dropped (the analyzer cannot catch a missing named argument on a constructor that doesn't require it).

Cheapest insurance while you are here: add `Model copyWith({int? contextWindow})` (or a focused `withContextWindow(int)`) next to the class and use it in both sites — then the field list lives exactly once, next to the class it mirrors.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "smol summarizer resolves the same number" claim is not implemented**

The registry's header doc says "main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx meter resolve the same number" — but the smol summarizer never touches the registry: `_compactChildIfNeeded` passes `rolesResolver?.resolveRole(smolModelRole)` straight into `AutoCompactorSources(smolModel:)` unwrapped, and the CLI's main compaction wiring does the same. sm-kicker.yml

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

- **PR #**: 1753
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1753
- **Title**: gh-1742 [GOAL] Truthful context pressure: compaction keyed to observed usage + honest windows (subagents ride fictitious windows today)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1742` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +2429
- **Deletions**: -290
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:28:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T20:41:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1742
### What changed
Context-pressure governance is now keyed to observed provider usage instead of the chars/4 estimate alone: pressure decisions reconcile `max(estimate, last observed input+cacheRead)`, all compaction surfaces resolve one shared per-model window registry, and headroom scales with the window instead of a flat 16k reserve.

### Key decisions
- New pure decision core `assessContextPressure` / `reconcileContextTokens` / `lastObservedContextTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/context_pressure.dart`): observed wins over estimate, estimate fills gaps; no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior.
- `ContextWindowRegistry` (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart`): one window per `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` shared by main, children, and the meter; `contextWindowCap` now applies to children too (previously `null` in `_compactChildIfNeeded`).
- `CompactionSettings.forWindow` proportional: reserve = `window/16` clamped to `[12.5k, 64k]`, keepRecent = `window/8` clamped to `[20k, 128k]` — a 1M window keeps ≥64k headroom instead of 1.6%. A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before.
- The CLI joins the shared registry: `AgentCli` owns one, `_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes endpoint reports, `/model-edit` publishes user pins, and `SubagentServices` hands it to the `task` tool — children spawned after a detection ride the served window, not the advertised one.
- Child compaction (`TaskExecutor._compactChildIfNeeded`): observed-over-headroom forces the pass through a per-child latch (`_forcedObservedAt`) so a stale pre-fold anchor cannot re-force every boundary.
- Fixed a real hole this exposed in `AutoCompactorFactory`: a FORCED structured run whose own estimate sat under the token trigger did zero passes yet reported `ok`, skipping the classic fallback — forced (usage- or message-cap-triggered) zero-pass outcomes now fall through to the classic engine, whose forced semantics actually run the summarizer.
- `SubagentHandle` pressure stamps carry `observedTokens` + `windowVerified` (AC6 badge basis for `task_status`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction test/task test/agent test/cli
```

<details><summary>Verification notes</summary>

- `test/compaction test/task test/agent test/hosts`: 1204 passed, 0 failed. `test/cli`: 3920 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (including the resume-parity marathon set and HEP compaction frames).
- The shared `browser_ext`/`integration` suites (subprocess/PTY-heavy, outside this ticket's surface) show runner-load flakiness (subprocess 2-minute timeouts) on this shared runner; no gh-1742-touched path is involved — CI on the PR is the authoritative gate for those.
</details>

<details><summary>AC coverage</summary>

- **AC1/AC5** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — reconciliation, forced-vs-estimate channels, edge `==` line.
- **AC2** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — registry published post-"detection" → child rides the registered window (131,072-vs-478k repro), cap clamps children.
- **AC2 (CLI)** `test/cli/agent_cli_context_window_registry_test.dart` — `/model-edit` publishes the pin; a child spawned after a registry entry resolves the registered window, not the carried one.
- **AC3** `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` — reserve/keep tables 8k→2M, clamps, monotonicity, legacy-parity floor in the ≤64k band.
- **AC4/REG-1** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — gh_1122 (never later than legacy at ≤200k) and kimi (−5% drift cannot delay the observed channel) regression pins at the real fixture scales.
- **AC5 IT** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — scripted gateway reporting `total_tokens` that excludes the cached prefix: estimate stays under the trigger while the forced pass demonstrably runs a compaction LLM call and lands a session compaction record.
</details>

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a confirming endpoint report still leaves the window "unverified"**

`_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes into the registry only when `detected != model.contextWindow`. When the endpoint's report CONFIRMS the carried catalog value (the common case for well-catalogued models), nothing is published, so `registry.isVerified(model)` stays false and the AC6 badge on every `task_status` pressure row marks that window unverified — even though the provider just verified it.

Since `publish` with the same value is a behavioral no-op (`windowFor` returns what the model already carries) and `withRegisteredContextWindow` short-circuits on `registered == model.contextWindow`, publishing unconditionally is free and makes the verification ladder honest:

```dart
if (detected != null) {
  _replaceModelLimits(
    contextWindow: detected == model.contextWindow ? null : detected,
    windowSource: ContextWindowSource.endpointReport,
  );
  ...
}
```

(with the publish reading `detected` rather than the rebuilt window, or by moving the publish next to the `detected != null` check). Purely a truth-in-UI fix; no behavior change.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

`withRegisteredContextWindow` rebuilds `Model` field-by-field (18 fields) to swap one value. This is the second hand-copy of the full field list in the codebase (`_replaceModelLimits` in `provider_models.dart` is the first); `Model` has no `copyWith`, so the next field added to `Model` (they do get added — `timeoutScopeLabel`, `capabilityNotes`, `connectTimeout`, `streamIdleTimeout` are all recent) must be remembered in **two** hand-copies plus anywhere else this pattern lands, or it is silently dropped (the analyzer cannot catch a missing named argument on a constructor that doesn't require it).

Cheapest insurance while you are here: add `Model copyWith({int? contextWindow})` (or a focused `withContextWindow(int)`) next to the class and use it in both sites — then the field list lives exactly once, next to the class it mirrors.

---

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1753
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1753
- **Title**: gh-1742 [GOAL] Truthful context pressure: compaction keyed to observed usage + honest windows (subagents ride fictitious windows today)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1742` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +2429
- **Deletions**: -290
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:28:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T20:41:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1742
### What changed
Context-pressure governance is now keyed to observed provider usage instead of the chars/4 estimate alone: pressure decisions reconcile `max(estimate, last observed input+cacheRead)`, all compaction surfaces resolve one shared per-model window registry, and headroom scales with the window instead of a flat 16k reserve.

### Key decisions
- New pure decision core `assessContextPressure` / `reconcileContextTokens` / `lastObservedContextTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/context_pressure.dart`): observed wins over estimate, estimate fills gaps; no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior.
- `ContextWindowRegistry` (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart`): one window per `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` shared by main, children, and the meter; `contextWindowCap` now applies to children too (previously `null` in `_compactChildIfNeeded`).
- `CompactionSettings.forWindow` proportional: reserve = `window/16` clamped to `[12.5k, 64k]`, keepRecent = `window/8` clamped to `[20k, 128k]` — a 1M window keeps ≥64k headroom instead of 1.6%. A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before.
- The CLI joins the shared registry: `AgentCli` owns one, `_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes endpoint reports, `/model-edit` publishes user pins, and `SubagentServices` hands it to the `task` tool — children spawned after a detection ride the served window, not the advertised one.
- Child compaction (`TaskExecutor._compactChildIfNeeded`): observed-over-headroom forces the pass through a per-child latch (`_forcedObservedAt`) so a stale pre-fold anchor cannot re-force every boundary.
- Fixed a real hole this exposed in `AutoCompactorFactory`: a FORCED structured run whose own estimate sat under the token trigger did zero passes yet reported `ok`, skipping the classic fallback — forced (usage- or message-cap-triggered) zero-pass outcomes now fall through to the classic engine, whose forced semantics actually run the summarizer.
- `SubagentHandle` pressure stamps carry `observedTokens` + `windowVerified` (AC6 badge basis for `task_status`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction test/task test/agent test/cli
```

<details><summary>Verification notes</summary>

- `test/compaction test/task test/agent test/hosts`: 1204 passed, 0 failed. `test/cli`: 3920 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (including the resume-parity marathon set and HEP compaction frames).
- The shared `browser_ext`/`integration` suites (subprocess/PTY-heavy, outside this ticket's surface) show runner-load flakiness (subprocess 2-minute timeouts) on this shared runner; no gh-1742-touched path is involved — CI on the PR is the authoritative gate for those.
</details>

<details><summary>AC coverage</summary>

- **AC1/AC5** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — reconciliation, forced-vs-estimate channels, edge `==` line.
- **AC2** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — registry published post-"detection" → child rides the registered window (131,072-vs-478k repro), cap clamps children.
- **AC2 (CLI)** `test/cli/agent_cli_context_window_registry_test.dart` — `/model-edit` publishes the pin; a child spawned after a registry entry resolves the registered window, not the carried one.
- **AC3** `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` — reserve/keep tables 8k→2M, clamps, monotonicity, legacy-parity floor in the ≤64k band.
- **AC4/REG-1** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — gh_1122 (never later than legacy at ≤200k) and kimi (−5% drift cannot delay the observed channel) regression pins at the real fixture scales.
- **AC5 IT** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — scripted gateway reporting `total_tokens` that excludes the cached prefix: estimate stays under the trigger while the forced pass demonstrably runs a compaction LLM call and lands a session compaction record.
</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1753._

> ℹ️ **7 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a confirming endpoint report still leaves the window "unverified"**

`_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes into the registry only when `detected != model.contextWindow`. When the endpoint's report CONFIRMS the carried catalog value (the common case for well-catalogued models), nothing is published, so `registry.isVerified(model)` stays false and the AC6 badge on every `task_status` pressure row marks that window unverified — even though the provider just verified it.

Since `publish` with the same value is a behavioral no-op (`windowFor` returns what the model already carries) and `withRegisteredContextWindow` short-circuits on `registered == model.contextWindow`, publishing unconditionally is free and makes the verification ladder honest:

```dart
if (detected != null) {
  _replaceModelLimits(
    contextWindow: detected == model.contextWindow ? null : detected,
    windowSource: ContextWindowSource.endpointReport,
  );
  ...
}
```

(with the publish reading `detected` rather than the rebuilt window, or by moving the publish next to the `detected != null` check). Purely a truth-in-UI fix; no behavior change.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

`withRegisteredContextWindow` rebuilds `Model` field-by-field (18 fields) to swap one value. This is the second hand-copy of the full field list in the codebase (`_replaceModelLimits` in `provider_models.dart` is the first); `Model` has no `copyWith`, so the next field added to `Model` (they do get added — `timeoutScopeLabel`, `capabilityNotes`, `connectTimeout`, `streamIdleTimeout` are all recent) must be remembered in **two** hand-copies plus anywhere else this pattern lands, or it is silently dropped (the analyzer cannot catch a missing named argument on a constructor that doesn't require it).

Cheapest insurance while you are here: add `Model copyWith({int? contextWindow})` (or a focused `withContextWindow(int)`) next to the class and use it in both sites — then the field list lives exactly once, next to the class it mirrors.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "smol summarizer resolves the same number" claim is not implemented**

The registry's header doc says "main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx meter resolve the same number" — but the smol summarizer never touches the registry: `_compactChildIfNeeded` passes `rolesResolver?.resolveRole(smolModelRole)` straight into `AutoCompactorSources(smolModel:)` unwrapped, and the CLI's main compaction wiring does the same. TDD rule: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". A VM segfault cannot be reproduced by a test — so changing production code would violate TDD. Do the PR's new tests list directories concurrently? The PR added test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart etc. — those use MemoryFileSystem mostly. Hmm.

Now, what's the RIGHT rework action per the rules?

- "Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup" — the root cause is a floating `sdk: stable` picking up a day-old SDK with a flaky VM race. # gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

## 3.15.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Language

Dart 3.15 allows [`this` to be type promoted][this-promotion-issue], just like
a local variable. To use this feature, set your package's
[SDK constraint][language version] lower bound to 3.15 or greater
(`sdk: '^3.15.0'`).

#### Type promotion of `this`

Previously, a type test or null check on `this` had no effect on its static
type, so code that wanted to take advantage of one had to copy `this` into a
local variable first:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    var self = this;
    if (self is Circle) print('radius ${self.radius}');
  }
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  final double radius;
  Circle(this.radius);
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    var self = this;
    if (self == null) return true;
    return self.isEven;
  }
}
```

Now `this` is promoted directly, and so is an implicit `this` in a member
access:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    if (this is Circle) print('radius $radius');
  }
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    if (this == null) return true;
    return isEven;
  }
}
```

The new [`unnecessary_this_alias`][unnecessary_this_alias] lint flags local
variables that only exist to work around the old behavior, and `dart fix` can
remove them.

[this-promotion-issue]: https://github.com/dart-lang/language/issues/1397
[language version]: https://dart.dev/to/language-version
[unnecessary_this_alias]: https://dart.dev/lints/unnecessary_this_alias

### Libraries

#### `dart:core`

- Added `double.maxSafeInteger` (`9007199254740991`, `2^53 - 1`) and
  `double.minSafeInteger` (`-9007199254740991`, `-(2^53 - 1)`).
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

#### `dart:math`

- Added `imul32(int a, int b)` for 32-bit signed wrapping multiplication.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

[#64491]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64491

### Tools

#### Analyzer

- When the value assigned through `operator []=` (in `a[i] = v`, `a[i] op= v`,
  `a[i] ??= v`, `a[i]++`, and so on) isn't assignable to the parameter type,
  the analyzer now reports `argument_type_not_assignable` instead of
  `invalid_assignment`, consistent with how it reports a non-assignable index.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64561][].

[#64561]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64561

#### Pub

- `dart pub publish` now creates reproducible `.tar.gz` package archives with
  deterministic entry ordering, zeroed modification timestamps, and normalized
  permissions ([dart-lang/pub#4885][]).
- On Windows, `dart pub` now requires `git.exe` on `PATH` and no longer invokes
  `git.cmd` or `git.bat` batch wrappers ([dart-lang/pub#4941][]).
- Deprecated the `--[no-]precompile` flag on `dart pub get`, `upgrade`, `add`,
  and `remove` ([dart-lang/pub#4910][]). `dart run` and `dart test` now cache
  precompiled executables directly in `.dart_tool/dartdev/bin/`.

[dart-lang/pub#4885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4885
[dart-lang/pub#4910]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4910
[dart-lang/pub#4941]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4941

## 3.14.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Libraries

#### `dart:ffi`

- Added `NativeFinalizer.callback`, which returns the finalization callback the
  finalizer was created with.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63811][]
- Added `Abi.iosArm64e` and `Abi.macosArm64e` for the `arm64e` architecture
  with pointer authentication on iOS and macOS.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63420][].

[#63420]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63420
[#63811]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63811

#### `dart:io`

- Process spawning on Mac switched from `fork`-and-`exec` to `posix_spawn`.
  `PATH` resolution will now happen with the parent's `PATH` instead of the
  child's `PATH`. Using an absolute path for the `executable` argument to
  `Process.start` etc is recommended to avoid platform-specific differences.

#### `dart:isolate`

- **Breaking change:** Unshipped the experimental synchronous execution and
  event loop control APIs (`Isolate.runSync`, `Isolate.create`,
  `Isolate.shutdownSync`, `Isolate.pinToCurrentThread`,
  `Isolate.isPinnedToCurrentThread`, `Isolate.runEventLoopSync`,
  `Isolate.onEvent`, and `Isolate.handleEvent`) that were accidentally exposed
  in Dart 3.13, and gated `NativeCallable.isolateGroupBound` behind the
  `--experimental-shared-data` VM flag.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64285][].

[#64285]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64285

#### `dart:typed_data`

- **Breaking change:** `toString()` on the SIMD value types `Float32x4`,
  `Int32x4` and `Float64x2` now returns `'V128'` instead of a list of the lane
  values. The old per-lane output was inconsistent across platforms and was
  never specified. On the VM this also covers `Error.safeToString` and the
  values shown by the debugger and the VM service.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63847][]
- **Breaking change:** `Float32x4.min`, `Float32x4.max`, `Float64x2.min`, and
  `Float64x2.max` now follow IEEE 754 semantics across all platforms: if either
  lane is `NaN`, the result lane is `NaN`, and `-0.0` is ordered below `+0.0`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63962][].
- Added `rangeEquals` extension methods on all integer typed data lists
  (`Uint8List`, `Int8List`, `Uint8ClampedList`, `Uint16List`, `Int16List`,
  `Uint32List`, `Int32List`, `Uint64List`, `Int64List`) and `ByteData` for
  efficient range equality comparisons.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64095][]

[#64095]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64095
- Added the bit-wise negation operator `~` to `Int32x4`, which inverts every bit
  of every lane.
- Added `Int32x4.splat`, which creates an `Int32x4` with the same 32-bit integer
  value in all four lanes, matching `Float32x4.splat` and `Float64x2.splat`.
- Added `Int32x4.equal`, a lane-wise equality comparison that returns `-1` in
  each lane where the operands are equal and `0` elsewhere, and the
  `Int32x4.anyTrue` getter, which is `true` when any lane is non-zero.
- Added `Int32x4.notEqual`, a lane-wise inequality comparison that returns `-1`
  in each lane where the operands differ and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.allTrue` getter, which is `true` only when every lane is
  non-zero.
- Added the signed lane-wise ordered comparisons `Int32x4.lessThan`,
  `Int32x4.lessThanOrEqual`, `Int32x4.greaterThan` and
  `Int32x4.greaterThanOrEqual`, each returning `-1` in lanes where the signed
  comparison holds and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.zero()` constructor, which creates an `Int32x4` with all
  four lanes set to zero.
- Added the unary negation operator `-` to `Int32x4`, which arithmetically
  negates each lane using two's complement.
- Added `Int32x4.abs`, which replaces each lane with its absolute value using
  two's complement, so the absolute value of the minimum 32-bit integer yields
  itself.
- Added the lane-wise shift operators `<<` (left), `>>` (arithmetic right) and
  `>>>` (logical right) to `Int32x4`.
- Added `Int32x4.andNot`, a lane-wise bit-wise and-not (`this & ~other`).
- Added `Int32x4.min`, which selects the smaller of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.
- Added `Int32x4.max`, which selects the larger of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.

[#63847]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63847
[#63962]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63962

#### `dart:js_interop`

- The `isA<JSArray>` check now uses both `Array.isArray` and `instanceof` to
  verify if a value is an array; it is considered an array if either condition
  returns true.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#62699][]

- Converting a `Future` to a `JSPromise` using `FutureOfJSAnyToJSPromise.toJS`
  or `FutureOfVoidToJSPromise.toJS` now passes JavaScript error
  values (`JSAny`) through directly to the rejected promise without
  wrapping them. Only Dart errors are wrapped in a JS `Error`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#61353][].

- Added extension methods `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartDoubleList` and
  `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartIntList` (`JSArrayOfJSNumberToList`);
  `List<num>.toJS` (`ListOfNumberToJSArray`);
  `JSArray<JSString>.toDartStringList` (`JSArrayOfJSStringToList`);
  `List<String>.toJS` (`ListOfStringToJSArray`);
  `JSArray<JSBoolean>.toDartBoolList` (`JSArrayOfJSBooleanToList`);
  `List<bool>.toJS` (`ListOfBoolToJSArray`);
  `JSArray<JSNumber?>.toDartDoubleList` and `JSArray<JSNumber?>.toDartIntList`
  (`JSArrayOfNullableJSNumberToList`); `List<num?>.toJS`
  (`ListOfNullableNumberToJSArray`); `JSArray<JSString?>.toDartStringList`
  (`JSArrayOfNullableJSStringToList`); `List<String?>.toJS`
  (`ListOfNullableStringToJSArray`); `JSArray<JSBoolean?>.toDartBoolList`
  (`JSArrayOfNullableJSBooleanToList`); and `List<bool?>.toJS`
  (`ListOfNullableBoolToJSArray`). These make it easier and more efficient to
  convert between JS and Dart arrays of primitives.

- Added `JSFunction.length` and `.name` getters.

- Added the `JSArray.fromAsync` static method to create an array from an
  asynchronous generator or a synchronous list of asynchronous values.

- Added `JSPromise.resolve` and `JSPromise.reject` static methods.

- Added extension methods `FutureOr<JSAny>.toJSPromiseOrValue`
  (`FutureOrToJSAny`), `FutureOr<JSAny?>.toJSPromiseOrValue`
  (`FutureOrToNullableJSAny`), `JSAny.toDartFutureOr` (`JSAnyToFutureOr`), and
  `JSAny?.toDartFutureOr` (`NullableJSAnyToFutureOr`). These make it easier and
  more efficient to convert between possibly-synchronous values at the Dart/JS
  boundary.

- Added extension methods `R Function(JSArray<E>).toJSVarArgs` and `R
  Function(T, JSArray<E>).toJSCaptureThisVarArgs` which capture JS function
  arguments as an array rather than as separate arguments to the Dart function.

- `Function.toJS` and `Function.toJSCaptureThis` now support functions without
  optional positional parameters that return `Future<T>` (where `T` is `void` or
  a subtype of `JSAny?`), automatically converting the returned `Future` to a
  `JSPromise`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63496][].

- `external` extension members can now be declared on generic type parameters
  bounded by a JS interop type (for example,
  `extension <T extends JSObject> on T`).
  For more details, see SDK issue [#61248][].

#### `dart:mirrors`

- The `dart:mirrors` library is now marked `@deprecated`, and will be removed
  in a future release. For details, see issue [#44489].

[#44489]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/44489
[#61248]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/61248
[#61353]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/61353
[#62699]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/62699
[#63496]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63496

### Tools

#### Analyzer

- Report an error (`js_interop_extension_constructor_js_annotation_has_no_effect`)
  when an `@JS` annotation is placed on an `external` constructor or factory of a
  `dart:js_interop` extension type, matching the CFE. Move the `@JS` annotation to
  the extension type declaration itself to rename non-object literal constructors.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#54366][].

[#54366]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/54366

#### Linter

- Added the `future_sync_value` lint rule, which recommends using
  `Future.syncValue` instead of `Future.sync` when the callback returns a
  synchronous (non-`Future`) value.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#61740][].

[#61740]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/61740

#### Dart CLI

- `dart run <package>:<command>` and `dart test` now cache the precompiled
  executable in `.dart_tool/dartdev/bin/` instead of `.dart_tool/pub/bin/`, and
  recompile it when any of its source files change. Previously the snapshot was
  rebuilt on every run for packages depended on by path, and could be stale for
  hosted packages with a path `dependency_override`.

- When `dart run <package>:<command>` and `dart test` run a precompiled
  executable, `Platform.script` now points at the Dart source file instead of
  the kernel snapshot. Resolving paths relative to `Platform.script` now works
  as it does when running from source.

- `dart run --enable-experiment=<experiment>` and
  `dart test --enable-experiment=<experiment>` now run from a snapshot compiled
  with those experiments, instead of falling back to running from source. The
  requested experiments still take effect, but startup is no longer slower than
  without them.

- Added a `dart migrate` command, which updates packages to a newer Dart SDK
  version. It raises the lower bound of each package's SDK constraint one minor
  version at a time. For each version, it applies preparatory fixes and raises
  the constraint. Optional cleanup fixes that adopt new language features only
  run with `--step=cleanup` or `--step=all`. Migrates the current directory by
  default, or specific package directories if provided. Packages must already
  require Dart 3.0 or later.
  - `--dry-run` previews the proposed changes.
  - `--apply` applies the changes.
  - `--target-sdk` migrates across multiple versions in one run.
  - `--step` runs specific steps: `prepare`, `bump`, `cleanup`, or `all`.
  - Dependent packages migrate together in lockstep, keeping dependency
    constraints solvable at every version. A package is skipped if a dependency
    does not support the new version.

  For more details, see SDK issue [#63240][].

- Added `-e` / `--eval` to `dart run` to evaluate inline Dart code snippets
  without creating a script file. Package imports are resolved from the current
  package configuration if present, or ephemerally on demand using `-P` /
  `--package-constraint` (for example, `dart run -P http:^1.0.0 -e '...'`) and
  `--offline`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64298][].

[#63240]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63240
[#64298]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64298

#### Formatter

- Enable experiments specified by surrounding `analysis_options.yaml` file when
  parsing code ([#1886][dart_style #1886]).

- Fix crash when formatting an enum with a primary constructor when trailing
  commas are preserved ([#1885][dart_style #1885]).

- Fix missing trailing comma on enum values when an enum has a primary
  constructor ([#1888][dart_style #1888]). Note that this style change is *not*
  language-versioned and also applies when formatting Dart 3.13 code.

- Fix crash when attempting to write a line with exactly 128 spaces of
  indentation.

[dart_style #1885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/dart_style/issues/1885
[dart_style #1886]: https://github.com/dart-lang/dart_style/issues/1886
[dart_style #1888]: https://github.com/dart-lang/dart_style/issues/1888

#### Pub

- `dart pub upgrade` now accepts `<package>@<constraint>`, `<package>@latest`,
  and `<package>@resolvable` targets to upgrade specific dependencies within a
  version constraint or inspect why a newer version cannot be selected
  (issue [dart-lang/pub#4569][]).

[dart-lang/pub#4569]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/issues/4569

#### dart2js

- Added the `--[no-]deprecated-js-interop` flag (`dart compile js` and
  `dart2js`). Passing `--no-deprecated-js-interop` disallows importing the
  deprecated JS interop libraries (`dart:html`, `dart:html_common`,
  `dart:indexed_db`, `dart:js`, `dart:js_util`, `dart:svg`, `dart:web_audio`,
  and `dart:web_gl`) and sets their `dart.library.*` environment conditions to
  `false` in conditional imports and `bool.fromEnvironment`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63919][].

#### Dart Development Compiler (dartdevc)

- Added the `--[no-]deprecated-js-interop` flag. Passing
  `--no-deprecated-js-interop` disallows importing the deprecated JS interop
  libraries (`dart:html`, `dart:html_common`, `dart:indexed_db`, `dart:js`,
  `dart:js_util`, `dart:svg`, `dart:web_audio`, and `dart:web_gl`) and sets
  their `dart.library.*` environment conditions to `false` in conditional
  imports and `bool.fromEnvironment`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63919][].

#### dart2wasm

- `dart2wasm` now emits standardized WebAssembly `try_table` exception handling
  instructions by default ([#54394][]).
- `dart2wasm` now requires native `wasm:js-string` built-in support and works
  around `WebAssembly.compileStreaming` bugs in Safari 26.5 and earlier
  ([#63543][]).
- `dart.library.isolate` now evaluates to `false` in conditional imports
  (`if (dart.library.isolate)`) when compiling with `dart2wasm` ([#64328][]).
- `dart compile wasm --standalone` no longer supports `dart:js_interop`.
- `Int32x4`, `Float32x4`, `Float64x2`, and their typed-data list views
  (`Int32x4List`, `Float32x4List`, `Float64x2List`) now compile to hardware
  128-bit WebAssembly SIMD (`v128`) instructions ([#64170][]).

[#54394]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/54394
[#63543]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63543
[#63919]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63919
[#64170]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64170
[#64328]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64328

## 3.13.3

**Released on:** 2026-09-01

This is a patch release that:

- Fixes an issue where Windows to Linux cross compilation
  produced incorrect executables if the applicatios used
  build hooks to link native code. (issue [#63953][])

[#63953]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63953

## 3.13.2

**Released on:** 2026-08-25

This is a patch release that:

- Fixes incorrect dart2wasm compilation of constructor invocations when
  the class was determined to be not allocatable. (issue [#63809][])
- Deprecates the legacy analyzer plugin system. (issue [#62164][])
- Fixes dart2js compiler crash when compiling code with
  nested constants in `record_use`. (issue [#64070][])
- Fixes a `dart format` crash and incorrect formatting with
  enums that use primary constructors.
  (issues [dart-lang/dart_style#1885][], [dart-lang/dart_style#1888][])

[#63809]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63809
[#62164]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/62164
[#64070]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64070

[dart-lang/dart_style#1885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/dart_style/issues/1885
[dart-lang/dart_style#1888]: https://github.com/dart-lang/dart_style/issues/1888


## 3.13.1

**Released on:** 2026-08-18

This is a patch release that:

- Fixes `dart fix --apply --code=migrate_design_widgets` to
  replace URIs in both import and export statements. (issue [#63968][])
- Fixes dart2wasm compiler crash in no-such-method forwarders.
  (issue [#63904][])
- Fixes dart2wasm compilation error if 3rd party `Type` implementations exist.
  (issue [#63843][])
- Fixes dart2wasm compiler crash if dynamic getter calls are used that
  target a getter implementation that was inferred to never return.
- Fixes dart2wasm compiler crash if named parameters in hierarchy have
