# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

## 3.15.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Language

Dart 3.15 allows [`this` to be type promoted][this-promotion-issue], just like
a local variable. To use this feature, set your package's
[SDK constraint][language version] lower bound to 3.15 or greater
(`sdk: '^3.15.0'`).

#### Type promotion of `this`

Previously, a type test or null check on `this` had no effect on its static
type, so code that wanted to take advantage of one had to copy `this` into a
local variable first:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    var self = this;
    if (self is Circle) print('radius ${self.radius}');
  }
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  final double radius;
  Circle(this.radius);
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    var self = this;
    if (self == null) return true;
    return self.isEven;
  }
}
```

Now `this` is promoted directly, and so is an implicit `this` in a member
access:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    if (this is Circle) print('radius $radius');
  }
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    if (this == null) return true;
    return isEven;
  }
}
```

The new [`unnecessary_this_alias`][unnecessary_this_alias] lint flags local
variables that only exist to work around the old behavior, and `dart fix` can
remove them.

[this-promotion-issue]: https://github.com/dart-lang/language/issues/1397
[language version]: https://dart.dev/to/language-version
[unnecessary_this_alias]: https://dart.dev/lints/unnecessary_this_alias

### Libraries

#### `dart:core`

- Added `double.maxSafeInteger` (`9007199254740991`, `2^53 - 1`) and
  `double.minSafeInteger` (`-9007199254740991`, `-(2^53 - 1)`).
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

#### `dart:math`

- Added `imul32(int a, int b)` for 32-bit signed wrapping multiplication.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

[#64491]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64491

### Tools

#### Analyzer

- When the value assigned through `operator []=` (in `a[i] = v`, `a[i] op= v`,
  `a[i] ??= v`, `a[i]++`, and so on) isn't assignable to the parameter type,
  the analyzer now reports `argument_type_not_assignable` instead of
  `invalid_assignment`, consistent with how it reports a non-assignable index.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64561][].

[#64561]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64561

#### Pub

- `dart pub publish` now creates reproducible `.tar.gz` package archives with
  deterministic entry ordering, zeroed modification timestamps, and normalized
  permissions ([dart-lang/pub#4885][]).
- On Windows, `dart pub` now requires `git.exe` on `PATH` and no longer invokes
  `git.cmd` or `git.bat` batch wrappers ([dart-lang/pub#4941][]).
- Deprecated the `--[no-]precompile` flag on `dart pub get`, `upgrade`, `add`,
  and `remove` ([dart-lang/pub#4910][]). `dart run` and `dart test` now cache
  precompiled executables directly in `.dart_tool/dartdev/bin/`.

[dart-lang/pub#4885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4885
[dart-lang/pub#4910]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4910
[dart-lang/pub#4941]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4941

## 3.14.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Libraries

#### `dart:ffi`

- Added `NativeFinalizer.callback`, which returns the finalization callback the
  finalizer was created with.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63811][]
- Added `Abi.iosArm64e` and `Abi.macosArm64e` for the `arm64e` architecture
  with pointer authentication on iOS and macOS.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63420][].

[#63420]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63420
[#63811]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63811

#### `dart:io`

- Process spawning on Mac switched from `fork`-and-`exec` to `posix_spawn`.
  `PATH` resolution will now happen with the parent's `PATH` instead of the
  child's `PATH`. Using an absolute path for the `executable` argument to
  `Process.start` etc is recommended to avoid platform-specific differences.

#### `dart:isolate`

- **Breaking change:** Unshipped the experimental synchronous execution and
  event loop control APIs (`Isolate.runSync`, `Isolate.create`,
  `Isolate.shutdownSync`, `Isolate.pinToCurrentThread`,
  `Isolate.isPinnedToCurrentThread`, `Isolate.runEventLoopSync`,
  `Isolate.onEvent`, and `Isolate.handleEvent`) that were accidentally exposed
  in Dart 3.13, and gated `NativeCallable.isolateGroupBound` behind the
  `--experimental-shared-data` VM flag.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64285][].

[#64285]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64285

#### `dart:typed_data`

- **Breaking change:** `toString()` on the SIMD value types `Float32x4`,
  `Int32x4` and `Float64x2` now returns `'V128'` instead of a list of the lane
  values. The old per-lane output was inconsistent across platforms and was
  never specified. On the VM this also covers `Error.safeToString` and the
  values shown by the debugger and the VM service.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63847][]
- **Breaking change:** `Float32x4.min`, `Float32x4.max`, `Float64x2.min`, and
  `Float64x2.max` now follow IEEE 754 semantics across all platforms: if either
  lane is `NaN`, the result lane is `NaN`, and `-0.0` is ordered below `+0.0`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63962][].
- Added `rangeEquals` extension methods on all integer typed data lists
  (`Uint8List`, `Int8List`, `Uint8ClampedList`, `Uint16List`, `Int16List`,
  `Uint32List`, `Int32List`, `Uint64List`, `Int64List`) and `ByteData` for
  efficient range equality comparisons.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64095][]

[#64095]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64095
- Added the bit-wise negation operator `~` to `Int32x4`, which inverts every bit
  of every lane.
- Added `Int32x4.splat`, which creates an `Int32x4` with the same 32-bit integer
  value in all four lanes, matching `Float32x4.splat` and `Float64x2.splat`.
- Added `Int32x4.equal`, a lane-wise equality comparison that returns `-1` in
  each lane where the operands are equal and `0` elsewhere, and the
  `Int32x4.anyTrue` getter, which is `true` when any lane is non-zero.
- Added `Int32x4.notEqual`, a lane-wise inequality comparison that returns `-1`
  in each lane where the operands differ and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.allTrue` getter, which is `true` only when every lane is
  non-zero.
- Added the signed lane-wise ordered comparisons `Int32x4.lessThan`,
  `Int32x4.lessThanOrEqual`, `Int32x4.greaterThan` and
  `Int32x4.greaterThanOrEqual`, each returning `-1` in lanes where the signed
  comparison holds and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.zero()` constructor, which creates an `Int32x4` with all
  four lanes set to zero.
- Added the unary negation operator `-` to `Int32x4`, which arithmetically
  negates each lane using two's complement.
- Added `Int32x4.abs`, which replaces each lane with its absolute value using
  two's complement, so the absolute value of the minimum 32-bit integer yields
  itself.
- Added the lane-wise shift operators `<<` (left), `>>` (arithmetic right) and
  `>>>` (logical right) to `Int32x4`.
- Added `Int32x4.andNot`, a lane-wise bit-wise and-not (`this & ~other`).
- Added `Int32x4.min`, which selects the smaller of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.
- Added `Int32x4.max`, which selects the larger of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.

[#63847]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63847
[#63962]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63962

#### `dart:js_interop`

- The `isA<JSArray>` check now uses both `Array.isArray` and `instanceof` to
  verify if a value is an array; it is considered an array if either condition
  returns true.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#62699][]

- Converting a `Future` to a `JSPromise` using `FutureOfJSAnyToJSPromise.toJS`
  or `FutureOfVoidToJSPromise.toJS` now passes JavaScript error
  values (`JSAny`) through directly to the rejected promise without
  wrapping them. Only Dart errors are wrapped in a JS `Error`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#61353][].

- Added extension methods `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartDoubleList` and
  `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartIntList` (`JSArrayOfJSNumberToList`);
  `List<num>.toJS` (`ListOfNumberToJSArray`);

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1753
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1753
- **Title**: gh-1742 [GOAL] Truthful context pressure: compaction keyed to observed usage + honest windows (subagents ride fictitious windows today)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1742` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +2429
- **Deletions**: -290
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:28:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T20:41:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1742
### What changed
Context-pressure governance is now keyed to observed provider usage instead of the chars/4 estimate alone: pressure decisions reconcile `max(estimate, last observed input+cacheRead)`, all compaction surfaces resolve one shared per-model window registry, and headroom scales with the window instead of a flat 16k reserve.

### Key decisions
- New pure decision core `assessContextPressure` / `reconcileContextTokens` / `lastObservedContextTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/context_pressure.dart`): observed wins over estimate, estimate fills gaps; no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior.
- `ContextWindowRegistry` (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart`): one window per `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` shared by main, children, and the meter; `contextWindowCap` now applies to children too (previously `null` in `_compactChildIfNeeded`).
- `CompactionSettings.forWindow` proportional: reserve = `window/16` clamped to `[12.5k, 64k]`, keepRecent = `window/8` clamped to `[20k, 128k]` — a 1M window keeps ≥64k headroom instead of 1.6%. A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before.
- The CLI joins the shared registry: `AgentCli` owns one, `_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes endpoint reports, `/model-edit` publishes user pins, and `SubagentServices` hands it to the `task` tool — children spawned after a detection ride the served window, not the advertised one.
- Child compaction (`TaskExecutor._compactChildIfNeeded`): observed-over-headroom forces the pass through a per-child latch (`_forcedObservedAt`) so a stale pre-fold anchor cannot re-force every boundary.
- Fixed a real hole this exposed in `AutoCompactorFactory`: a FORCED structured run whose own estimate sat under the token trigger did zero passes yet reported `ok`, skipping the classic fallback — forced (usage- or message-cap-triggered) zero-pass outcomes now fall through to the classic engine, whose forced semantics actually run the summarizer.
- `SubagentHandle` pressure stamps carry `observedTokens` + `windowVerified` (AC6 badge basis for `task_status`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction test/task test/agent test/cli
```

<details><summary>Verification notes</summary>

- `test/compaction test/task test/agent test/hosts`: 1204 passed, 0 failed. `test/cli`: 3920 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (including the resume-parity marathon set and HEP compaction frames).
- The shared `browser_ext`/`integration` suites (subprocess/PTY-heavy, outside this ticket's surface) show runner-load flakiness (subprocess 2-minute timeouts) on this shared runner; no gh-1742-touched path is involved — CI on the PR is the authoritative gate for those.
</details>

<details><summary>AC coverage</summary>

- **AC1/AC5** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — reconciliation, forced-vs-estimate channels, edge `==` line.
- **AC2** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — registry published post-"detection" → child rides the registered window (131,072-vs-478k repro), cap clamps children.
- **AC2 (CLI)** `test/cli/agent_cli_context_window_registry_test.dart` — `/model-edit` publishes the pin; a child spawned after a registry entry resolves the registered window, not the carried one.
- **AC3** `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` — reserve/keep tables 8k→2M, clamps, monotonicity, legacy-parity floor in the ≤64k band.
- **AC4/REG-1** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — gh_1122 (never later than legacy at ≤200k) and kimi (−5% drift cannot delay the observed channel) regression pins at the real fixture scales.
- **AC5 IT** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — scripted gateway reporting `total_tokens` that excludes the cached prefix: estimate stays under the trigger while the forced pass demonstrably runs a compaction LLM call and lands a session compaction record.
</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1753._

> ℹ️ **7 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,

name: Flake watch

on:

    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues

## 3.15.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Language

Dart 3.15 allows [`this` to be type promoted][this-promotion-issue], just like
a local variable. To use this feature, set your package's
[SDK constraint][language version] lower bound to 3.15 or greater
(`sdk: '^3.15.0'`).

#### Type promotion of `this`

Previously, a type test or null check on `this` had no effect on its static
type, so code that wanted to take advantage of one had to copy `this` into a
local variable first:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    var self = this;
    if (self is Circle) print('radius ${self.radius}');
  }
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  final double radius;
  Circle(this.radius);
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    var self = this;
    if (self == null) return true;
    return self.isEven;
  }
}
```

Now `this` is promoted directly, and so is an implicit `this` in a member
access:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    if (this is Circle) print('radius $radius');
  }
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    if (this == null) return true;
    return isEven;
  }
}
```

The new [`unnecessary_this_alias`][unnecessary_this_alias] lint flags local
variables that only exist to work around the old behavior, and `dart fix` can
remove them.

[this-promotion-issue]: https://github.com/dart-lang/language/issues/1397
[language version]: https://dart.dev/to/language-version
[unnecessary_this_alias]: https://dart.dev/lints/unnecessary_this_alias

### Libraries

#### `dart:core`

- Added `double.maxSafeInteger` (`9007199254740991`, `2^53 - 1`) and
  `double.minSafeInteger` (`-9007199254740991`, `-(2^53 - 1)`).
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

#### `dart:math`

- Added `imul32(int a, int b)` for 32-bit signed wrapping multiplication.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

[#64491]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64491

### Tools

#### Analyzer

- When the value assigned through `operator []=` (in `a[i] = v`, `a[i] op= v`,
  `a[i] ??= v`, `a[i]++`, and so on) isn't assignable to the parameter type,
  the analyzer now reports `argument_type_not_assignable` instead of
  `invalid_assignment`, consistent with how it reports a non-assignable index.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64561][].

[#64561]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64561

#### Pub

- `dart pub publish` now creates reproducible `.tar.gz` package archives with
  deterministic entry ordering, zeroed modification timestamps, and normalized
  permissions ([dart-lang/pub#4885][]).
- On Windows, `dart pub` now requires `git.exe` on `PATH` and no longer invokes
  `git.cmd` or `git.bat` batch wrappers ([dart-lang/pub#4941][]).
- Deprecated the `--[no-]precompile` flag on `dart pub get`, `upgrade`, `add`,
  and `remove` ([dart-lang/pub#4910][]). `dart run` and `dart test` now cache
  precompiled executables directly in `.dart_tool/dartdev/bin/`.

[dart-lang/pub#4885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4885
[dart-lang/pub#4910]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4910
[dart-lang/pub#4941]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4941

## 3.14.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Libraries

#### `dart:ffi`

- Added `NativeFinalizer.callback`, which returns the finalization callback the
  finalizer was created with.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63811][]
- Added `Abi.iosArm64e` and `Abi.macosArm64e` for the `arm64e` architecture
  with pointer authentication on iOS and macOS.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63420][].

[#63420]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63420
[#63811]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63811

#### `dart:io`

- Process spawning on Mac switched from `fork`-and-`exec` to `posix_spawn`.
  `PATH` resolution will now happen with the parent's `PATH` instead of the
  child's `PATH`. Using an absolute path for the `executable` argument to
  `Process.start` etc is recommended to avoid platform-specific differences.

#### `dart:isolate`

- **Breaking change:** Unshipped the experimental synchronous execution and
  event loop control APIs (`Isolate.runSync`, `Isolate.create`,
  `Isolate.shutdownSync`, `Isolate.pinToCurrentThread`,
  `Isolate.isPinnedToCurrentThread`, `Isolate.runEventLoopSync`,
  `Isolate.onEvent`, and `Isolate.handleEvent`) that were accidentally exposed
  in Dart 3.13, and gated `NativeCallable.isolateGroupBound` behind the
  `--experimental-shared-data` VM flag.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64285][].

[#64285]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64285

#### `dart:typed_data`

- **Breaking change:** `toString()` on the SIMD value types `Float32x4`,
  `Int32x4` and `Float64x2` now returns `'V128'` instead of a list of the lane
  values. The old per-lane output was inconsistent across platforms and was
  never specified. On the VM this also covers `Error.safeToString` and the
  values shown by the debugger and the VM service.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63847][]
- **Breaking change:** `Float32x4.min`, `Float32x4.max`, `Float64x2.min`, and
  `Float64x2.max` now follow IEEE 754 semantics across all platforms: if either
  lane is `NaN`, the result lane is `NaN`, and `-0.0` is ordered below `+0.0`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63962][].
- Added `rangeEquals` extension methods on all integer typed data lists
  (`Uint8List`, `Int8List`, `Uint8ClampedList`, `Uint16List`, `Int16List`,
  `Uint32List`, `Int32List`, `Uint64List`, `Int64List`) and `ByteData` for
  efficient range equality comparisons.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64095][]

[#64095]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64095
- Added the bit-wise negation operator `~` to `Int32x4`, which inverts every bit
  of every lane.
- Added `Int32x4.splat`, which creates an `Int32x4` with the same 32-bit integer
  value in all four lanes, matching `Float32x4.splat` and `Float64x2.splat`.
- Added `Int32x4.equal`, a lane-wise equality comparison that returns `-1` in
  each lane where the operands are equal and `0` elsewhere, and the
  `Int32x4.anyTrue` getter, which is `true` when any lane is non-zero.
- Added `Int32x4.notEqual`, a lane-wise inequality comparison that returns `-1`
  in each lane where the operands differ and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.allTrue` getter, which is `true` only when every lane is
  non-zero.
- Added the signed lane-wise ordered comparisons `Int32x4.lessThan`,
  `Int32x4.lessThanOrEqual`, `Int32x4.greaterThan` and
  `Int32x4.greaterThanOrEqual`, each returning `-1` in lanes where the signed
  comparison holds and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.zero()` constructor, which creates an `Int32x4` with all
  four lanes set to zero.
- Added the unary negation operator `-` to `Int32x4`, which arithmetically
  negates each lane using two's complement.
- Added `Int32x4.abs`, which replaces each lane with its absolute value using
  two's complement, so the absolute value of the minimum 32-bit integer yields
  itself.
- Added the lane-wise shift operators `<<` (left), `>>` (arithmetic right) and
  `>>>` (logical right) to `Int32x4`.
- Added `Int32x4.andNot`, a lane-wise bit-wise and-not (`this & ~other`).
- Added `Int32x4.min`, which selects the smaller of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.
- Added `Int32x4.max`, which selects the larger of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.

[#63847]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63847
[#63962]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63962

#### `dart:js_interop`

- The `isA<JSArray>` check now uses both `Array.isArray` and `instanceof` to
  verify if a value is an array; it is considered an array if either condition
  returns true.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#62699][]

- Converting a `Future` to a `JSPromise` using `FutureOfJSAnyToJSPromise.toJS`
  or `FutureOfVoidToJSPromise.toJS` now passes JavaScript error
  values (`JSAny`) through directly to the rejected promise without
  wrapping them. Only Dart errors are wrapped in a JS `Error`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#61353][].

- Added extension methods `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartDoubleList` and
  `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartIntList` (`JSArrayOfJSNumberToList`);
  `List<num>.toJS` (`ListOfNumberToJSArray`);

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1753._

> ℹ️ **7 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a confirming endpoint report still leaves the window "unverified"**

`_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes into the registry only when `detected != model.contextWindow`. When the endpoint's report CONFIRMS the carried catalog value (the common case for well-catalogued models), nothing is published, so `registry.isVerified(model)` stays false and the AC6 badge on every `task_status` pressure row marks that window unverified — even though the provider just verified it.

Since `publish` with the same value is a behavioral no-op (`windowFor` returns what the model already carries) and `withRegisteredContextWindow` short-circuits on `registered == model.contextWindow`, publishing unconditionally is free and makes the verification ladder honest:

```dart
if (detected != null) {
  _replaceModelLimits(
    contextWindow: detected == model.contextWindow ? null : detected,
    windowSource: ContextWindowSource.endpointReport,
  );
  ...
}
```

(with the publish reading `detected` rather than the rebuilt window, or by moving the publish next to the `detected != null` check). Purely a truth-in-UI fix; no behavior change.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

`withRegisteredContextWindow` rebuilds `Model` field-by-field (18 fields) to swap one value. This is the second hand-copy of the full field list in the codebase (`_replaceModelLimits` in `provider_models.dart` is the first); `Model` has no `copyWith`, so the next field added to `Model` (they do get added — `timeoutScopeLabel`, `capabilityNotes`, `connectTimeout`, `streamIdleTimeout` are all recent) must be remembered in **two** hand-copies plus anywhere else this pattern lands, or it is silently dropped (the analyzer cannot catch a missing named argument on a constructor that doesn't require it).

Cheapest insurance while you are here: add `Model copyWith({int? contextWindow})` (or a focused `withContextWindow(int)`) next to the class and use it in both sites — then the field list lives exactly once, next to the class it mirrors.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "smol summarizer resolves the same number" claim is not implemented**

The registry's header doc says "main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx meter resolve the same number" — but the smol summarizer never touches the registry: `_compactChildIfNeeded` passes `rolesResolver?.resolveRole(smolModelRole)` straight into `AutoCompactorSources(smolModel:)` unwrapped, and the CLI's main compaction wiring does the same. So: a transient Dart VM segfault under runner load. This is the classic infra-flake signature. The no-op loop guard warns against dismissing owned violations as infra, but ci_violations.json itself reports owned: 0 — nothing is owned. The 2 unknowns are (a) the aggregate leg's exit-1 (pure consequence of the hostile-env crash) and (b) the hostile-env exit-134 VM crash itself.

What CAN this rework do that's honest and useful?

Option A: Push nothing; write response.md + empty review_replies.json; classify the red as infra/SDK-internal with evidence, and note validation re-dispatches on the current head. Risk: "a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked" — but there are NO open threads (0 at rework start, confirmed by review_state.md + the raw census). Round 2 did exactly this (empty replies) and it was accepted (the discussion shows "✅ Rework finished" after round 2... wait, actually the round-2 pass DID push d3b6ba6fc8 — the AC-R3 test fix. So this lap (round 3) faces: 0 open threads, 1 infra-flake CI red.

Options:
1. **No code change, document** — response.md explains: threads 0, CI red is a VM-internal flake (evidence), no owned violations; validation re-runs on the head. But the bot message said "rework re-queued ... The rework runner pushes a fix and validation re-runs on the new head (validate-fresh)". If no new head is pushed, does validation re-run? Per gh-917: "first validation included, review or no review" and "red yields the slot — after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head". The red head d3b6ba6f is red 1/3. So a new head would re-arm validation.

2. **Push a small, legitimate hardening change** that gives validation a new head. What would be legitimate and not invented scope? TDD rule: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". A VM segfault cannot be reproduced by a test — so changing production code would violate TDD. Changing CI config (sdk pin) is "config" fix per FIX_CI ("Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup").

Hmm, actually — wait. Let me reconsider whether the crash is *really* random. Directory.list race... The crash happened at 20:35:31, right after `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` completed... but tests run concurrently, so the "last completed" tells little. Do the PR's new tests list directories concurrently? The PR added test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart etc. — those use MemoryFileSystem mostly. Hmm.

Not attributable to the PR's diff (which touches compaction/task/CLI window plumbing; no dart:io directory-walk changes — the diff grep showed no `Directory.` usage).

Now, what's the RIGHT rework action per the rules?

- "Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup" — the root cause is a floating `sdk: stable` picking up a day-old SDK with a flaky VM race. Pining one leg to 3.13.5 would itself deviate from the repo's convention AND age badly (the pin would silently rot). The repo has a `flake-watch.yml` workflow — the project's stance on flakes is to watch/re-run them, not to pin.

Let me check if there's an established re-run/retry mechanism for CI legs (ci.yml retry hints, flake-watch, or a re-run convention) — because the cheapest correct "fix" might be to re-run the failed leg, and the rework's job is then to push... hmm, but re-running is the SM/validation's job.

So the expectation: rework pushes (any new head) → validation re-runs on the new head. If I push nothing, validation may stay parked on the red head (red 1/3; after 3 reds it waits for a new head — we're at 1/3, so validation *could* re-dispatch... but gh-917 says rework armed → validation re-runs on the NEW head after the rework pushes a fix).

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

## 3.15.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Language

Dart 3.15 allows [`this` to be type promoted][this-promotion-issue], just like
a local variable. To use this feature, set your package's
[SDK constraint][language version] lower bound to 3.15 or greater
(`sdk: '^3.15.0'`).

#### Type promotion of `this`

Previously, a type test or null check on `this` had no effect on its static
type, so code that wanted to take advantage of one had to copy `this` into a
local variable first:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    var self = this;
    if (self is Circle) print('radius ${self.radius}');
  }
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  final double radius;
  Circle(this.radius);
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    var self = this;
    if (self == null) return true;
    return self.isEven;
  }
}
```

Now `this` is promoted directly, and so is an implicit `this` in a member
access:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    if (this is Circle) print('radius $radius');
  }
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    if (this == null) return true;
    return isEven;
  }
}
```

The new [`unnecessary_this_alias`][unnecessary_this_alias] lint flags local
variables that only exist to work around the old behavior, and `dart fix` can
remove them.

[this-promotion-issue]: https://github.com/dart-lang/language/issues/1397
[language version]: https://dart.dev/to/language-version
[unnecessary_this_alias]: https://dart.dev/lints/unnecessary_this_alias

### Libraries

#### `dart:core`

- Added `double.maxSafeInteger` (`9007199254740991`, `2^53 - 1`) and
  `double.minSafeInteger` (`-9007199254740991`, `-(2^53 - 1)`).
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

#### `dart:math`

- Added `imul32(int a, int b)` for 32-bit signed wrapping multiplication.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

[#64491]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64491

### Tools

#### Analyzer

- When the value assigned through `operator []=` (in `a[i] = v`, `a[i] op= v`,
  `a[i] ??= v`, `a[i]++`, and so on) isn't assignable to the parameter type,
  the analyzer now reports `argument_type_not_assignable` instead of
  `invalid_assignment`, consistent with how it reports a non-assignable index.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64561][].

[#64561]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64561

#### Pub

- `dart pub publish` now creates reproducible `.tar.gz` package archives with
  deterministic entry ordering, zeroed modification timestamps, and normalized
  permissions ([dart-lang/pub#4885][]).
- On Windows, `dart pub` now requires `git.exe` on `PATH` and no longer invokes
  `git.cmd` or `git.bat` batch wrappers ([dart-lang/pub#4941][]).
- Deprecated the `--[no-]precompile` flag on `dart pub get`, `upgrade`, `add`,
  and `remove` ([dart-lang/pub#4910][]). `dart run` and `dart test` now cache
  precompiled executables directly in `.dart_tool/dartdev/bin/`.

[dart-lang/pub#4885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4885
[dart-lang/pub#4910]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4910
[dart-lang/pub#4941]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4941

## 3.14.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Libraries

#### `dart:ffi`

- Added `NativeFinalizer.callback`, which returns the finalization callback the
  finalizer was created with.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63811][]
- Added `Abi.iosArm64e` and `Abi.macosArm64e` for the `arm64e` architecture
  with pointer authentication on iOS and macOS.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63420][].

[#63420]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63420
[#63811]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63811

#### `dart:io`

- Process spawning on Mac switched from `fork`-and-`exec` to `posix_spawn`.
  `PATH` resolution will now happen with the parent's `PATH` instead of the
  child's `PATH`. Using an absolute path for the `executable` argument to
  `Process.start` etc is recommended to avoid platform-specific differences.

#### `dart:isolate`

- **Breaking change:** Unshipped the experimental synchronous execution and
  event loop control APIs (`Isolate.runSync`, `Isolate.create`,
  `Isolate.shutdownSync`, `Isolate.pinToCurrentThread`,
  `Isolate.isPinnedToCurrentThread`, `Isolate.runEventLoopSync`,
  `Isolate.onEvent`, and `Isolate.handleEvent`) that were accidentally exposed
  in Dart 3.13, and gated `NativeCallable.isolateGroupBound` behind the
  `--experimental-shared-data` VM flag.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64285][].

[#64285]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64285

#### `dart:typed_data`

- **Breaking change:** `toString()` on the SIMD value types `Float32x4`,
  `Int32x4` and `Float64x2` now returns `'V128'` instead of a list of the lane
  values. The old per-lane output was inconsistent across platforms and was
  never specified. On the VM this also covers `Error.safeToString` and the
  values shown by the debugger and the VM service.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63847][]
- **Breaking change:** `Float32x4.min`, `Float32x4.max`, `Float64x2.min`, and
  `Float64x2.max` now follow IEEE 754 semantics across all platforms: if either
  lane is `NaN`, the result lane is `NaN`, and `-0.0` is ordered below `+0.0`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63962][].
- Added `rangeEquals` extension methods on all integer typed data lists
  (`Uint8List`, `Int8List`, `Uint8ClampedList`, `Uint16List`, `Int16List`,
  `Uint32List`, `Int32List`, `Uint64List`, `Int64List`) and `ByteData` for
  efficient range equality comparisons.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64095][]

[#64095]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64095
- Added the bit-wise negation operator `~` to `Int32x4`, which inverts every bit
  of every lane.
- Added `Int32x4.splat`, which creates an `Int32x4` with the same 32-bit integer
  value in all four lanes, matching `Float32x4.splat` and `Float64x2.splat`.
- Added `Int32x4.equal`, a lane-wise equality comparison that returns `-1` in
  each lane where the operands are equal and `0` elsewhere, and the
  `Int32x4.anyTrue` getter, which is `true` when any lane is non-zero.
- Added `Int32x4.notEqual`, a lane-wise inequality comparison that returns `-1`
  in each lane where the operands differ and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.allTrue` getter, which is `true` only when every lane is
  non-zero.
- Added the signed lane-wise ordered comparisons `Int32x4.lessThan`,
  `Int32x4.lessThanOrEqual`, `Int32x4.greaterThan` and

- Added the unary negation operator `-` to `Int32x4`, which arithmetically
  negates each lane using two's complement.
- Added `Int32x4.abs`, which replaces each lane with its absolute value using
  two's complement, so the absolute value of the minimum 32-bit integer yields
  itself.
- Added the lane-wise shift operators `<<` (left), `>>` (arithmetic right) and
  `>>>` (logical right) to `Int32x4`.
- Added `Int32x4.andNot`, a lane-wise bit-wise and-not (`this & ~other`).
- Added `Int32x4.min`, which selects the smaller of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.
- Added `Int32x4.max`, which selects the larger of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.

- name: IT — piped wizard under dash/busybox/bash (AC2-AC5)
        run: dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:

```cpp
DirectoryListingEntry::~DirectoryListingEntry() { ResetLink(); }
...
void DirectoryListingEntry::ResetLink() {
 if (link_length == 0 && (link != NULL)) { free(link); link = NULL; }
``

Important correction: the 19:45 hostile-env run (3964172951, head 143ee1e036) ALSO ran **3.13.6** — and it did NOT segfault (it failed on the real AC-R3 test, then completed the suite). So 3.13.6 is not deterministically crashing; the segfault is a **flaky race** that hit once (20:27–20:35 run) out of the two 3.13.6 hostile-env executions. Same tree (well, 143ee1e036 vs d3b6ba6f — one test file changed) passed the full suite at 19:45 on the same SDK.

Additional evidence for flakiness:
- Same run: all 4 "Core tests" shards passed on 3.13.6 (the same suite, split in 4, run with the same `dart test` machinery + same SDK).
- The crash is in an IO-service worker thread with zero package frames.

So: a transient Dart VM segfault under runner load. This is the classic infra-flake signature. The no-op loop guard warns against dismissing owned violations as infra, but ci_violations.json itself reports owned: 0 — nothing is owned. The 2 unknowns are (a) the aggregate leg's exit-1 (pure consequence of the hostile-env crash) and (b) the hostile-env exit-134 VM crash itself.

What CAN this rework do that's honest and useful?

Option A: Push nothing; write response.md + empty review_replies.json; classify the red as infra/SDK-internal with evidence, and note validation re-dispatches on the current head. Risk: "a pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked" — but there are NO open threads (0 at rework start, confirmed by review_state.md + the raw census). Round 2 did exactly this (empty replies) and it was accepted (the discussion shows "✅ Rework finished" after round 2... wait, actually the round-2 pass DID push d3b6ba6fc8 — the AC-R3 test fix. The "Rework Complete — pr-1753" comment is round 2's).

Hmm wait, actually let me re-check: round 2 pushed d3b6ba6fc8 ("gh-1742 review round 2: AC-R3 resume-budget test tracks the corrected curve") which is HEAD. Validation then ran on d3b6ba6fc8 → hostile-env segfault → merge aborted, rework re-queued (this lap, round 3).

So this lap (round 3) faces: 0 open threads, 1 infra-flake CI red.

Options:
1. **No code change, document** — response.md explains: threads 0, CI red is a VM-internal flake (evidence), no owned violations; validation re-runs on the head. But the bot message said "rework re-queued ... The rework runner pushes a fix and validation re-runs on the new head (validate-fresh)". If no new head is pushed, does validation re-run? Per gh-917: "first validation included, review or no review" and "red yields the slot — after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head". The red head d3b6ba6f is red 1/3. So a new head would re-arm validation.

2. **Push a small, legitimate hardening change** that gives validation a new head. What would be legitimate and not invented scope? TDD rule: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". A VM segfault cannot be reproduced by a test — so changing production code would violate TDD. Changing CI config (sdk pin) is "config" fix per FIX_CI ("Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup").

Hmm, actually — wait. Let me reconsider whether the crash is *really* random. Directory.list race... What if the PR's code (or its tests) do heavy concurrent Directory listing that didn't exist before? The crash happened at 20:35:31, right after `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` completed... but tests run concurrently, so the "last completed" tells little. The IO thread crash could belong to ANY in-flight test.

Do the PR's new tests list directories concurrently? The PR added test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart etc. — those use MemoryFileSystem mostly. Hmm.

But here's the thing: the SAME suite ran fully green on the same SDK at 19:45 (hostile-env, head 143ee1e036 — that tree contains ALL of the PR's new tests except the AC-R3 test rewrite) and again — 4/4 core shards green on the same SDK at 20:27 (tree d3b6ba6f, full suite INCLUDING the new tests, just sharded). So the PR's tests ran on 3.13.6 at least five times (4 shards + hostile@19:45) without the segfault, and hit it once at 20:27 under the hostile-env leg's single-process full-suite run (which is the most loaded, longest single `dart test` invocation — 11.6k tests, ~8 min, most concurrency).

Verdict: transient VM-internal crash (SDK 3.13.6, dart::bin Directory::List race), 1 hit in ~6 executions of the same suite on this SDK, zero test failures, zero package frames. Not attributable to the PR's diff (which touches compaction/task/CLI window plumbing; no dart:io directory-walk changes — the diff grep showed no `Directory.` usage).

Now, what's the RIGHT rework action per the rules?

- "Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup" — the root cause is a floating `sdk: stable` picking up a day-old SDK with a flaky VM race. A **config fix** would be: pin the hostile-env leg (or all legs) to a known-good SDK. But ALL 22 legs float on stable by convention, and the crash is rare (1/6). Pining one leg to 3.13.5 would itself deviate from the repo's convention AND age badly (the pin would silently rot). The repo has a `flake-watch.yml` workflow — the project's stance on flakes is to watch/re-run them, not to pin.

Let me check if there's an established re-run/retry mechanism for CI legs (ci.yml retry hints, flake-watch, or a re-run convention) — because the cheapest correct "fix" might be to re-run the failed leg, and the rework's job is then to push... hmm, but re-running is the SM/validation's job.

Actually — hold on. Let me re-read the rework arming message: "⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head — merge aborted, rework re-queued. (linked issue #1742 re-armed) (approval latch kept — no re-review after fixes) ... The rework runner pushes a fix and validation re-runs on the new head (validate-fresh)."

So the expectation: rework pushes (any new head) → validation re-runs on the new head. If I push nothing, validation may stay parked on the red head (red 1/3; after 3 reds it waits for a new head — we're at 1/3, so validation *could* re-dispatch... but gh-917 says rework armed → validation re-runs on the NEW head after the rework pushes a fix).

Given the operational contract ("red yields the slot... The rework runner pushes a fix and validation re-runs on the new head"), the pragmatic and honest move: make a **minimal, legitimately-justified change** so validation gets a fresh head, and re-verify locally. What minimal change is genuinely justified by THIS red?

Ideas:
a) Pin the hostile-env leg's Dart SDK — deviates from convention, ages badly, and pins-against-flakes is the opposite of the repo's flake-watch stance. Also the same SDK passed 5/6 times; pining to 3.13.5 (already superseded) is questionable.

b) No production/test change; instead, document + push an empty-ish commit? Forbidden ("never invent work", and an empty commit is dishonest).

c) Treat it as what it is — infra flake — and RE-RUN the failed leg via gh (actions re-run). The repo has precedent? Let me check how the project handles VM-crash flakes... flake-watch.yml. Let me read it.

Actually, wait. Let me also check the OTHER two reds (Binaries smoke gate, JS engine integration on the kicker run) — jobs with no steps, 404 logs, run conclusion success. Those are required-check shims that failed likely because... hmm, "kicker" workflow with jobs named exactly like CI checks: "Quality gate", "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate". These look like *mirror* jobs in the kicker workflow that proxy the CI results for branch protection. They failed with no steps = probably `gh run watch`-style proxy jobs that timed out waiting for the CI run, or were failed intentionally when the CI run failed (propagation). Since the CI run failed (hostile-env), the proxies failing is consistent — same root cause.

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

## 3.15.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Language

Dart 3.15 allows [`this` to be type promoted][this-promotion-issue], just like
a local variable. To use this feature, set your package's
[SDK constraint][language version] lower bound to 3.15 or greater
(`sdk: '^3.15.0'`).

#### Type promotion of `this`

Previously, a type test or null check on `this` had no effect on its static
type, so code that wanted to take advantage of one had to copy `this` into a
local variable first:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    var self = this;
    if (self is Circle) print('radius ${self.radius}');
  }
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  final double radius;
  Circle(this.radius);
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    var self = this;
    if (self == null) return true;
    return self.isEven;
  }
}
```

Now `this` is promoted directly, and so is an implicit `this` in a member
access:

```dart
class Shape {
  void describe() {
    if (this is Circle) print('radius $radius');
  }
}

extension on int? {
  bool get isEvenOrNull {
    if (this == null) return true;
    return isEven;
  }
}
```

The new [`unnecessary_this_alias`][unnecessary_this_alias] lint flags local
variables that only exist to work around the old behavior, and `dart fix` can
remove them.

[this-promotion-issue]: https://github.com/dart-lang/language/issues/1397
[language version]: https://dart.dev/to/language-version
[unnecessary_this_alias]: https://dart.dev/lints/unnecessary_this_alias

### Libraries

#### `dart:core`

- Added `double.maxSafeInteger` (`9007199254740991`, `2^53 - 1`) and
  `double.minSafeInteger` (`-9007199254740991`, `-(2^53 - 1)`).
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

#### `dart:math`

- Added `imul32(int a, int b)` for 32-bit signed wrapping multiplication.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64491][].

[#64491]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64491

### Tools

#### Analyzer

- When the value assigned through `operator []=` (in `a[i] = v`, `a[i] op= v`,
  `a[i] ??= v`, `a[i]++`, and so on) isn't assignable to the parameter type,
  the analyzer now reports `argument_type_not_assignable` instead of
  `invalid_assignment`, consistent with how it reports a non-assignable index.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64561][].

[#64561]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64561

#### Pub

- `dart pub publish` now creates reproducible `.tar.gz` package archives with
  deterministic entry ordering, zeroed modification timestamps, and normalized
  permissions ([dart-lang/pub#4885][]).
- On Windows, `dart pub` now requires `git.exe` on `PATH` and no longer invokes
  `git.cmd` or `git.bat` batch wrappers ([dart-lang/pub#4941][]).
- Deprecated the `--[no-]precompile` flag on `dart pub get`, `upgrade`, `add`,
  and `remove` ([dart-lang/pub#4910][]). `dart run` and `dart test` now cache
  precompiled executables directly in `.dart_tool/dartdev/bin/`.

[dart-lang/pub#4885]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4885
[dart-lang/pub#4910]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4910
[dart-lang/pub#4941]: https://github.com/dart-lang/pub/pull/4941

## 3.14.0

**Released on:** Unreleased

### Libraries

#### `dart:ffi`

- Added `NativeFinalizer.callback`, which returns the finalization callback the
  finalizer was created with.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63811][]
- Added `Abi.iosArm64e` and `Abi.macosArm64e` for the `arm64e` architecture
  with pointer authentication on iOS and macOS.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63420][].

[#63420]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63420
[#63811]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63811

#### `dart:io`

- Process spawning on Mac switched from `fork`-and-`exec` to `posix_spawn`.
  `PATH` resolution will now happen with the parent's `PATH` instead of the
  child's `PATH`. Using an absolute path for the `executable` argument to
  `Process.start` etc is recommended to avoid platform-specific differences.

#### `dart:isolate`

- **Breaking change:** Unshipped the experimental synchronous execution and
  event loop control APIs (`Isolate.runSync`, `Isolate.create`,
  `Isolate.shutdownSync`, `Isolate.pinToCurrentThread`,
  `Isolate.isPinnedToCurrentThread`, `Isolate.runEventLoopSync`,
  `Isolate.onEvent`, and `Isolate.handleEvent`) that were accidentally exposed
  in Dart 3.13, and gated `NativeCallable.isolateGroupBound` behind the
  `--experimental-shared-data` VM flag.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64285][].

[#64285]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64285

#### `dart:typed_data`

- **Breaking change:** `toString()` on the SIMD value types `Float32x4`,
  `Int32x4` and `Float64x2` now returns `'V128'` instead of a list of the lane
  values. The old per-lane output was inconsistent across platforms and was
  never specified. On the VM this also covers `Error.safeToString` and the
  values shown by the debugger and the VM service.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63847][]
- **Breaking change:** `Float32x4.min`, `Float32x4.max`, `Float64x2.min`, and
  `Float64x2.max` now follow IEEE 754 semantics across all platforms: if either
  lane is `NaN`, the result lane is `NaN`, and `-0.0` is ordered below `+0.0`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#63962][].
- Added `rangeEquals` extension methods on all integer typed data lists
  (`Uint8List`, `Int8List`, `Uint8ClampedList`, `Uint16List`, `Int16List`,
  `Uint32List`, `Int32List`, `Uint64List`, `Int64List`) and `ByteData` for
  efficient range equality comparisons.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#64095][]

[#64095]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64095
- Added the bit-wise negation operator `~` to `Int32x4`, which inverts every bit
  of every lane.
- Added `Int32x4.splat`, which creates an `Int32x4` with the same 32-bit integer
  value in all four lanes, matching `Float32x4.splat` and `Float64x2.splat`.
- Added `Int32x4.equal`, a lane-wise equality comparison that returns `-1` in
  each lane where the operands are equal and `0` elsewhere, and the
  `Int32x4.anyTrue` getter, which is `true` when any lane is non-zero.
- Added `Int32x4.notEqual`, a lane-wise inequality comparison that returns `-1`
  in each lane where the operands differ and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.allTrue` getter, which is `true` only when every lane is
  non-zero.
- Added the signed lane-wise ordered comparisons `Int32x4.lessThan`,
  `Int32x4.lessThanOrEqual`, `Int32x4.greaterThan` and
  `Int32x4.greaterThanOrEqual`, each returning `-1` in lanes where the signed
  comparison holds and `0` elsewhere.
- Added the `Int32x4.zero()` constructor, which creates an `Int32x4` with all
  four lanes set to zero.
- Added the unary negation operator `-` to `Int32x4`, which arithmetically
  negates each lane using two's complement.
- Added `Int32x4.abs`, which replaces each lane with its absolute value using
  two's complement, so the absolute value of the minimum 32-bit integer yields
  itself.
- Added the lane-wise shift operators `<<` (left), `>>` (arithmetic right) and
  `>>>` (logical right) to `Int32x4`.
- Added `Int32x4.andNot`, a lane-wise bit-wise and-not (`this & ~other`).
- Added `Int32x4.min`, which selects the smaller of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.
- Added `Int32x4.max`, which selects the larger of each pair of lanes,
  compared as signed 32-bit integers.

[#63847]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63847
[#63962]: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63962

#### `dart:js_interop`

- The `isA<JSArray>` check now uses both `Array.isArray` and `instanceof` to
  verify if a value is an array; it is considered an array if either condition
  returns true.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#62699][]

- Converting a `Future` to a `JSPromise` using `FutureOfJSAnyToJSPromise.toJS`
  or `FutureOfVoidToJSPromise.toJS` now passes JavaScript error
  values (`JSAny`) through directly to the rejected promise without
  wrapping them. Only Dart errors are wrapped in a JS `Error`.
  For more details, see SDK issue [#61353][].

- Added extension methods `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartDoubleList` and
  `JSArray<JSNumber>.toDartIntList` (`JSArrayOfJSNumberToList`);
  `List<num>.toJS` (`ListOfNumberToJSArray`);

- name: IT — piped wizard under dash/busybox/bash (AC2-AC5)

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache

          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). gh-1537: the watcher consumes PR-dispatch runs only
# (workflow_dispatch events) — the post-merge main CI trigger is retired,
# and a red v* tag run is a release-flow failure (daily-publish triage),
# never a flake to quarantine. The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .
